Today’s challenges in the digital age demand more than theory. They demand clarity, critical thinking and the ability to adapt.

This is the driving force behind RappLearn, the learning and training arm of Rappler, built to equip emerging professionals, leaders, and organizations with global insight and skills shaped by real-world experience.

RappLearn is a growing ecosystem of executive masterclasses, workshops, and experiences led by award-winning journalists, technologists, and policy experts at the forefront of today’s biggest conversations, from AI to information integrity to storytelling and governance.

Currently, it operates across two formats, online and in person, offering expertly designed masterclasses and experiences alongside access to an exclusive peer community through the Rappler app, connecting learners across industries and sectors.

AI. Professionals from various sectors gain foundational knowledge and hands-on guidance in using generative AI during RappLearn’s workshop, where they learn to use select AI tools and explore strategies to integrate them responsibly while keeping decision-making human-centered and safeguarding critical thinking, on February 28, 2026, at the Rappler newsroom.

Learning with Rappler

At its core, RappLearn is built for people who want to move forward: professionals and leaders seeking sharper thinking, and a community grounded in growth.

Anchored on Rappler’s award-winning journalism, RappLearn’s approach to training is shaped by real-world experience at the frontlines of today’s most urgent challenges — from disinformation to AI and public trust.

Because of this, RappLearn extends far beyond media and journalism training, and equips industries and organizations across all sectors with the tools to lead responsibly and intelligently in this changing world.

Explore the current offerings below.

Executive Masterclass on AI and Governance

Best for senior leaders, professionals, and organizations across all industries

WORKSHOP. Gemma Mendoza, Rappler’s Head of Digital Services and Lead Researcher on Disinformation and Platforms, leads the Creating a people-first AI Policy Tech Xperience Workshop, at the Social Good Summit on November 16, 2025.

“That Rappler workshop scared me to death about AI. Rappler taught me how to use AI, but they also made me realize how easily it can be abused,” remarked veteran economist Winnie Monsod after attending one of Rappler’s AI Masterclasses at the Rappler HQ. That tension, between risk and opportunity, is precisely where Rappler’s AI Masterclasses are anchored.

The AI Executive Masterclass, “Work Better, Think Smarter in the Age of AI,” is a high-level workshop designed to turn AI overwhelm into operational clarity.

Participants engage in a dynamic curriculum designed to help leaders from varying industries learn the fundamentals of generative AI, gain hands-on experience with AI tools, and explore ways to keep learning and working in a human-centered way.

This fee-based program offers individual slots for fixed cohorts or customized institutional training for organizations. In tailored sessions, teams can go a step further with “Crafting and Implementing AI Policies that Work,” a module dedicated to defining “red lines,” assigning governance roles, and embedding ethical checks directly into organizational workflows.

Organizations who have attended our programs come from a wide range of industries and sectors. These include academic institutions such as Far Eastern University, PHINMA Education, Metro Dumaguete College, and Wesleyan University Philippines; business groups and non-profit organizations such as Negros Occidental Chamber of Commerce and Industry, AboitizPower, and Bonifacio Art Foundation Inc., as well as other civil society groups.

Learn more about the current schedule here.

Tailored Executive Workshops

Best for corporate teams, business groups, government agencies, and civil society

RappLearn provides customized programs that help teams lead with integrity and speak with authority. These sessions are tailored to address unique organizational challenges in digital transformation and high-impact communication.

Institutional training packages may include, but are not limited to, any of the following:

Strategic writing and communications for organizations

Using data to tell compelling stories

Digital storytelling in the modern world

Creating effective short-form videos

Media training (featuring real-world simulations for high-stakes interviews and how to deal with the media)

Crisis management

AI POLICY LAB. Staff from the Consuelo Foundation join RappLearn’s team-based workshop on March 7, 2026, at the Rappler newsroom to gain foundational knowledge and hands-on guidance in using generative AI, participating in a collaborative session to draft values-based policies that ensure AI use remains ethical, responsible, and human-centered.

Immersive Newsroom learning experiences

Best for high school, college students, and educators

The Newsroom learning experience (which can be designed as a tour, visit, or immersion) is a one-day experiential program that brings students and educators into the Rappler newsroom to experience the realities of professional journalism.

Participants move beyond textbooks to observe news gathering and distribution in a high-risk digital environment. The curriculum is flexible, with modules and workshop topics tailored to the visiting group’s objectives, covering everything and anything about journalism, media ethics, fact-checking, community engagement, among others.

NEWSROOM IMMERSION. Over 100 senior high school students from San Beda College Alabang take over the Rappler newsroom for an immersion, where they learn what it truly means to report stories, verify information, and stand for truth. At a time when algorithms blur the line between content and credible journalism, conversations like these matter more than ever.

A central focus of the session is helping participants appreciate the fundamental difference between professional journalism and content creation. By exploring the ethical standards of accuracy and accountability, the program clarifies the distinction between being a “journalist” and being an “influencer.”

This fee-based newsroom learning experience also offers a facilitated workshop where learners produce their own multimedia content, applying newsroom principles to navigate today’s information landscape with integrity.

Schools that have participated include San Beda College Alabang Integrated K-12 Department and Technical High School, Visayas State University, and Ilocos Sur Polytechnic State College–Sta Maria Campus, among others.

Led by practitioners and experts in the field

RappLearn’s trainings are facilitated by active practitioners navigating today’s digital challenges, including Chay Hofileña, Rappler’s head of training, a veteran investigative editor, and academic lecturer; Gemma Mendoza, an award-winning investigative journalist and Rappler’s lead researcher on platforms and disinformation who pioneers projects connecting data with citizen action; and Don Kevin Hapal, an expert in AI strategy and digital forensics from The Nerve, a digital forensics consultancy born from Rappler’s investigative work on disinformation.

INSIDE THE NEWSROOM. Veteran journalist and Rappler Managing Editor Miriam Grace Go engages with San Beda College Alabang Integrated K-12 Department and Technical High School students during the school’s newsroom immersion at the Rappler newsroom on March 23.

Beyond this core team, RappLearn’s programs also draw on the specialized expertise of other Rappler professionals across various units — from newsroom and data research to community engagement and creative production, ensuring every session is grounded in current, cross-functional newsroom practices.

Ready to transform your team? Email us at learn@rappler.com. – Rappler.com

World.title: FULL TEXT: Marcos’ opening statement at 48th ASEAN Summit plenary session
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

PLENARY. Southeast Asian leaders gather for the 48th ASEAN Summit plenary session in Cebu on May 8, 2026.

'Today, we gather to confront, with unity and resolve, the repercussions of the situation in the Middle East,' says Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

CEBU, Philippines – Collective action among member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations “has never been more urgent” in light of the massive economic disruptions caused by the Middle East war, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told his fellow ASEAN leaders on Friday, May 8.

In his opening statement during the 48th ASEAN Summit plenary session in Cebu, Marcos zeroed in on three priorities: ensuring regional energy security and resilience, stabilizing food security, and upholding the safety of ASEAN nationals.

Read Marcos’ opening statement in full below.

Your Majesty,

Excellencies,

Distinguished Colleagues,

My ASEAN brothers and sisters,

Good morning.

It is my pleasure to welcome you to the 48th ASEAN Summit Plenary.

I also take the opportunity to congratulate His Excellency Prime Minister Lê Minh Hưng on his election as Prime Minister of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam, and warmly welcome him to the ASEAN Summit.

I also wish to extend my warmest congratulations to His Excellency Sonexay Siphandone on his re-election as Prime Minister of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic.

And in the same spirit, let me likewise extend my warmest congratulations to His Excellency Mr. Anutin Charnvirakul on his re-election as Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand.

We meet at a defining moment for our region and the global community.

The international geopolitical landscape continues to be marked by uncertainty and heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly, by the grave situation in the Middle East.

ASEAN has expressed serious concern over the escalation of conflict due to the preemptive attacks initiated by Israel and the United States against the Islamic Republic of Iran on February 28, 2026, and the subsequent retaliatory attacks by Iran against several countries in the region.

These developments have disrupted maritime and air transport routes, heightened risks to merchant and non-combatant vessels and aircraft, and affected the flow of energy and essential goods.

Against this backdrop, we come together guided by ASEAN’s long-standing commitment to peace, and the collective positions expressed by each ASEAN Member State:

– the immediate cessation of hostilities;

– the peaceful settlement of disputes;

– the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure; and

– the restoration of safe, unimpeded, and continuous transit passage in the Strait of Hormuz.

For ASEAN, these challenges are deeply felt by our people — through higher living costs, supply disruptions, threatened livelihoods, economic strain, [and] growing vulnerability, both in our homelands and amongst our nationals in the Middle East.

It is a stark reminder that, in an increasingly uncertain world, we call for our collective action and it has never been more urgent so we must continue to uphold the principles of ASEAN centrality and solidarity and pursue practical cooperation.

For this, I thank you for answering the call, underscoring the importance and urgency of convening at this time.

It is in this spirit that we gather today to pursue concrete outcomes and forge a collective path with particular focus on three urgent and interrelated priorities.

First, we must ensure regional energy security and resilience.

At a time of heightened volatility, ASEAN must strengthen coordination and reinforce preparedness, [and] pursue practical collective measures to safeguard a stable energy supply and improve interconnectivity, all the while advancing alternative and renewable energy sources to protect our economies from further shocks and to respond to the urgent challenge of climate change.

In this effort, we must also harness innovation, including inclusive and responsible applications of artificial intelligence, to improve energy forecasting, strengthen grid management and system flexibility, and support the clean energy transition.

Second, we must work together to stabilize food security.

Disruptions in trade and transport stemming from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz quickly affected food prices and supply, especially fertilizers, and subsequently, the welfare of our peoples.

Our task is to ensure that ASEAN remains responsive, to strengthen and expand intra-ASEAN trade, and build the capacities to safeguard and fortify our food systems across the region.

Digital innovation can help us anticipate shortages, improve agricultural productivity, and support responsive decision-making so that our peoples in vulnerable situations are better protected.

Third, we must uphold the safety of ASEAN nationals.

In moments of crisis, ASEAN solidarity must be measured by our ability to act in concert to safeguard our peoples, wherever they may be.

This means strengthening early warning systems, enhancing consular coordination, and ensuring the timely delivery of assistance through the prudent use of new technologies, including exploring how AI-enabled tools may advance our priorities, anchored in human judgment and international law.

Play Video

Today, we gather to confront, with unity and resolve, the repercussions of the situation in the Middle East, and seek to advance our common commitment to peace, stability, and prosperity while ensuring that the benefits of our cooperation are felt by all our peoples.

In this regard, the Philippines, as Chair, reaffirms its strong commitment to steering ASEAN through changing and uncertain times under our Chairship theme, “Navigating Our Future, Together.”

As we push forward the first year of the implementation of the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, we are reminded that our region is strongest when we turn shared challenges, however daunting they may be, into shared purpose.

And to this end, we recognize the importance of maritime cooperation and look forward to the adoption of the ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on Maritime Cooperation, which includes the Philippines’ proposal to establish an ASEAN Maritime Centre, which will serve as an important platform for maritime cooperation in coordination with relevant ASEAN and ASEAN-led mechanisms.

“Navigating Our Future, Together” is not only our Chairship theme, but also the task that lies ahead of us.

With this, I have the honor to declare the 48th ASEAN Summit Plenary now open.

– Rappler.com

World.title: Apple, Meta warn Canadian bill could force them to weaken encryption
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

Canada's Bill C-22 is part of a broader push by governments to expand lawful access to encrypted data, a move tech companies say risks weakening user security

Apple and Meta have publicly opposed a Canadian bill that the companies say could require them to break the encryption of their devices and services if passed.

Bill C-22 was proposed by Canada’s ruling Liberal Party, which gained a parliamentary majority last month and is currently being debated in the House of Commons. Canadian law enforcement officials say the bill would help them investigate security threats earlier and act more quickly.

It is part of a broader push by governments to expand lawful access to encrypted data, a move tech companies say risks weakening user security.

The Canadian bill contains provisions that, depending on how they are implemented, could be similar to a UK data access provision order sent to Apple last year. That order prompted Apple to withdraw a feature allowing users to store data in its cloud with end-to-end encryption.

US officials later said Britain had dropped the request after the US director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, raised concerns it could violate a cloud data treaty.

End-to-end encryption means that only the user — not even Apple, Meta or law enforcement — can access the data without a key. The technology is widely used in services such as Meta Platforms’ WhatsApp and Apple’s iMessage, and security experts say it provides powerful protections against spying and cybercrime.

“At a time of rising and pervasive threats from malicious actors seeking access to user information, Bill C-22, as drafted, would undermine our ability to offer the powerful privacy and security features users expect from Apple,” Apple said in a statement. “This legislation could allow the Canadian government to force companies to break encryption by inserting backdoors into their products – something Apple will never do.”

In prepared testimony, Meta’s head of public policy for Canada, Rachel Curran, and Privacy and Public Policy Director Robyn Greene said the bill’s “sweeping powers, minimal oversight, and lack of clear safeguards” could make Canadians less safe, rather than more.

“As drafted, the bill could require companies like Meta to build or maintain capabilities that break, weaken, or circumvent encryption or other zero-knowledge security architectures, and force providers to install government spyware directly on their systems,” the two wrote.

In an email, Tim Warmington, a spokesperson for Public Safety Canada, said the law would not require technology firms to make changes that introduce a “systemic vulnerability” into electronic protections such as encryption.

“They know their systems and have a vested interest in keeping them secure,” Warmington said.

The US Office of the Director of National Intelligence did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the bill. – Rappler.com

World.title: Marcos urges fellow ASEAN leaders to ensure regional energy, food security
World.content:
Watch the opening statement of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. during the 48th ASEAN Summit plenary session here

CEBU, Philippines – Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. opened the 48th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit plenary session on Friday, May 8, with a call to strengthen regional coordination to ensure stable energy and food supply.

Marcos noted that trade and transport disruptions caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure affected global food prices and supply, particularly fertilizer prices.

The Philippine President said that ASEAN leaders’ task now is to boost renewable energy sources to protect economies from further shocks, and to expand trade within the regional bloc to safeguard food systems across the region.

“In an increasingly uncertain world, we call for our collective action and it has never been more urgent so we must continue to uphold the principles of ASEAN centrality and solidarity and pursue practical cooperation,” he added.

World.content:
Rappler's Bea Cupin walks you through the context of events unfolding in the 48th ASEAN Summit

CEBU, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. gathers leaders and representatives of the 11 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states in Mactan Island in Cebu on Friday, May 8, for the first leaders-level meeting under the Philippines’ chairmanship.

Even as most meetings are moved online and the 48th ASEAN Summit was made “austere” in the face of economic disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, the Philippines has set lofty ambitions: to think of ways to shield ASEAN from crises stemming from geopolitical tensions and to rally together a bloc that operates solely on consensus.

World.title: FACT CHECK: No free electricity, subsidies for national ID, vaccine card holders
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

PhilSys debunked the claim in a May 7 post, saying that having a national ID does not mean automatic qualification for financial aid. No government office has announced such benefits for COVID-19 vaccine card holders either.

Claim: Filipinos with a national ID or a vaccine card can avail themselves of free electricity and various subsidies by completing an online registration form.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: Various posts making claims like these have been circulating on Facebook, mostly posted by pages that present themselves as news outlets, such as “PH Daily News Alert” and “Serbisyong Tapat News.”

The most popular post has garnered 991,000 views, 14,000 reactions, and 3,500 shares as of writing. This post, along with similar ones posted by other pages, uses video of a supposed news anchor claiming that vaccine card holders can claim free electricity and subsidies every month by filling out a registration form.

A similar tactic has been used in videos claiming that the same benefits apply to national ID holders, with one video reaching over 57,000 views.

The facts: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) debunked the claim in a May 7 Facebook post, saying that there is no truth to these claims and that they did not come from the PSA.

“Ang pagkakaroon ng National ID ay hindi nangangahulugan ng awtomatikong pagtanggap ng anumang uri ng ayuda o assistance,” the agency wrote. “Ang pagbibigay ng benepisyo ay nananatiling nakabatay sa umiiral na patakaran, proseso, at kwalipikasyon ng bawat ahensya na nagpapatupad ng mga programang ito.”

(Having a National ID does not automatically qualify a person for receiving any type of aid or assistance. The granting of these benefits is based on existing policies, processes, and qualifications of each agency implementing these programs.)

No government office or credible news outlets announced such benefits for COVID-19 vaccine card holders either.

The supposed news reports are also 99% likely to be AI-generated, according to AI detection tool SightEngine.

Phishing risk: Link scanner urlscan.io shows that the links attached to the viral posts lead to blog sites posing as government update websites. Official websites of the Philippine government use a gov.ph domain, unlike the links contained in the fake post.

Phishing link checker EasyDMARC found the blog sites suspicious for phishing. This means filling out the form may pose risks to users’ personal and financial information. (READ: Phishing 101: How to spot and avoid phishing)

Free electricity: The false posts circulated amid heated online discussions on subsidies for the electricity bills of low-income households and senior citizens. (

Rappler has also debunked other claims about fake government assistance programs:

– Shay Du/Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: No SC order blocking 2026 impeachment proceedings vs Duterte
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

While Duterte earlier filed a petition asking the SC to block the impeachment proceedings against her, the High Court did not issue a temporary restraining order

Claim: The Supreme Court (SC) issued an order blocking the renewed impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook post bearing the claim has already received 1,300 reactions, 379 comments, and 161 shares as of writing. It was posted on April 28 amid the House justice committee hearing on Duterte’s impeachment.

The post shows a composite photo of Duterte, House justice committee chair Gerville Luistro, House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima, and House justice committee members Terry Ridon and Joel Chua. A photo of the SC is also included in the middle, showing SC justices such as Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.

The text on the photo reads, “Lahat napahiya! Impeachment pinatigil na? Korte nagdisisyon na! Naglabas ng ultimatom sa Kamara?”

(Everyone is embarrassed! Has the impeachment been stopped? The Court has already decided! Issued an ultimatum to the House?)

Many social media users believed the claim, with comments thanking the Supreme Court for its supposed decision to block the impeachment.

The facts: The SC did not issue any order blocking the new impeachment proceedings against Duterte. While the Vice President earlier filed a petition with the SC asking it to block the impeachment proceedings against her, she failed to secure a temporary restraining order from the High Court, allowing the House justice panel to continue its public hearing on her impeachment case.

Six days after the false claim was posted, the House justice panel approved its report containing the resolution setting forth the articles of impeachment against Duterte.

In January 2026, the High Court affirmed the unconstitutionality of the previous impeachment case against Duterte for violating the one-year bar rule. However, this ruling does not affect the current impeachment proceedings against the Vice President.

Rappler has recently debunked a similar post falsely claiming that the SC has dismissed the impeachment case against Duterte.

Latest updates: After a series of House justice committee hearings, the impeachment complaint against Duterte has been elevated to the House plenary, with the plenary vote expected on May 11. (READ: More than required number of lawmakers seen to vote for Sara Duterte impeachment)

Securing one-third support from House members would impeach Duterte for the second time. The impeachment articles will then be transmitted to the Senate, which will convene itself as an impeachment court for a trial.

The Vice President is accused of misusing public funds, amassing ill-gotten wealth, and making death threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

World.title: 4 new fire inspectors relieved for shady practices — DILG chief
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — At least four new Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) fire inspectors have been relieved from their posts for purported questionable practices, Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said on Friday.

“Slowly, we are dismantling their system,” he told reporters at the Kapihan ng Samahang Plaridel in Manila on Friday.

“The new fire inspectors who came here had body cameras when they operated. If anyone complained, we’d act on it quickly. Since then, we’ve caught four more inspectors,” he detailed.

Article continues after this 

READ: DILG sues BFP chief over P14-M ‘kickbacks’

Last March, all BFP National Capital Region (NCR) fire inspectors were relieved from their posts, reassigned to farther regions, and replaced with fire inspectors from other areas as part of the DILG’s new crackdown on questionable practices in the agency.

Remulla previously cited that many fire inspectors were forcing business owners to purchase fire extinguishers from suppliers linked to them, charging fees for full firefighting services, and extorting money from applicants seeking to enter the bureau.

Asked about the offenses of the four newly-caught inspectors, Remulla answered that he could only clearly recall one case: that of a BFP NCR inspector — whom he did not name — who allegedly sought P40,000 from a Valle Verde, Pasig City resident to release their home’s fire inspection permit.

“That’s what the BFP got accustomed to. It seemed like their kingdom, their right to extort. It stops now,” Remulla stressed.

Article continues after this 

“We can stop it. It will take time, but we are almost there,” he said. /das

Article continues after this

World.title: Lacson: Marcoleta said a lot, but didn’t deny seeking P500-M allocables
World.content:
Senate President Pro Tempore Panfilo Lacson (left) and Sen. Rodante Marcoleta. — INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Rodante Marcoleta has said a lot of things during his most recent privilege speech, but he did not deny the existence of an alleged handwritten letter containing his request for P500 million worth of allocables from the executive, Senate President Pro Tempore Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said.

Lacson, in a statement, said that Marcoleta may have deliberately missed out on responding to the “most important” issue — that of a handwritten note left by Undersecretary Maria Catalina Cabral of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) addressed to a “Cong. Marcoleta.”

“He ‘deliberately’ missed the most important reaction: deny or refute the handwritten note (c/o Cong Marcoleta) on the document as presented,” Lacson said in a post on X.

Article continues after this 

Lacson was referring to the privilege speech from Marcoleta on Wednesday, which was an answer to the partial report of the Senate blue ribbon committee that Lacson chaired, and to his statements over different interviews.

READ: Lacson: Cabral’s handwritten note shows P500M ‘allocables’ for Marcoleta

Part of Lacson’s report showed that Marcoleta supposedly received P500 million in “allocables” or items in the DPWH budget, which are placed in certain projects that a lawmaker prefers.

Lacson, the chairman of the Senate blue ribbon committee, said a day after he unveiled portions of the partial report on the flood control probe.

“There is a handwritten note from the late Undersecretary Cabral indicating that she made allocations based on requests for the allocable funds. She was able to allocate P500 million worth of projects to Senator Marcoleta,” Lacson told a dzBB radio interview.

Article continues after this 

This letter, he said, is not yet with the Office of the Ombudsman, and he plans to submit the document, which came directly from Cabral’s camp.

“Cong. Marcoleta” may refer to two individuals: Senator Marcoleta, who was a member of the 19th Congress, and his son, incumbent Sagip party-list Rep. Paolo Henry Marcoleta, who is in his first term after the 2025 elections.

Article continues after this 

However, since the issues being discussed are related to the 2025 national budget, which was crafted in 2024, only Senator Marcoleta was part of Congress during that time.

In a later press conference, Lacson clarified that the project allocables to Marcoleta have not yet been linked to ghost or substandard infrastructure projects.

READ: Marcoleta urges Lacson to invite Romualdez to flood control probe

On Wednesday, Marcoleta delivered his own privilege speech, claiming that the statements made by Lacson failed to present the complete picture and failed to provide the proper context.

“It was spliced, not the whole picture, and it has no sufficient context, and it seems to refer to this representation that I asked for projects amounting to 500, whether it’s P500 billion, P500 million, or P500 thousand. The big document tells a narrative that a certain Cong. Marcoleta has this P500 (million) allocation for the DPWH,” Marcoleta said in his speech.

“It seems that his privileged speech at the session hall was not enough, and they had to widen its scope through the media to ensure that malicious insinuations would be spread, even if it lacked clarity and substance,” he added.

Marcoleta pointed out that when Lacson said almost all senators of the 19th Congress made insertions using allocables, Lacson’s “buddy,” Senate President Vicente Sotto III, said this is not an automatic indication of corruption.

“But our President, you Mr. President yourself, defended the senators and said that ‘I would like to make it clear that whatever budgetary amendments the senators propose, the money for these projects does not in any way go through the Senate or the senator as some of our kababayans think. It goes directly to the implementing agencies and the Executive Department,’” Marcoleta said.

“With the many names dragged into this controversy — some of which our chairman appears to be carefully avoiding and were not mentioned directly, even if they are repeatedly linked by witnesses through their sworn affidavits — I am being forcefully dragged into his narrative. This is too obvious,” he added. /das

World.title: Sara, Castro swap barbs: ‘Attention-seeker,’ ‘VP can’t do research’
World.content:
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro (left) and Vice President Sara Duterte — File photos

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte and Palace press officer Claire Castro exchanged yet more heated remarks, with the former calling the latter an “attention-seeker” and the latter saying that the former apparently cannot research what is currently happening in the country.

These recent statements stemmed from an interview with Duterte at The Hague, Netherlands, on Thursday, May 7 (Netherlands time), wherein she was asked about Castro’s recent statement that the vice president’s “demeanor” when answering questions about her preparedness for the upcoming 2028 presidential elections, in which she recently declared she would run.

READ: Palace: Sara Duterte’s 2028 polls ‘prayer’ baseless, mere intrigue

Article continues after this 

“I always say, that when Claire Castro speaks, don’t pay attention or give it importance. Because if you pay attention, you feed her attention-seeking habit,” Duterte said.

“And the problem with that is with her attention-seeking habit, she will bring shame to our country. Because when she speaks, there is the seal of the Office Of the President. That means, the whole world that is watching and listening seems to think that this Philippines is a poor country. Because this is how the speaker is,” she added.

When asked for her response to Duterte’s remark against her, Castro said in an ambush interview in the international media center in Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu, that she is not an “attention-seeker” since she only answers questions from the media.

“We are not giving any statement that is not in line with the Palace. And if she doesn’t want to pay attention to me, there’s nothing I can do. I’m not paying attention to her because she’s not the one asking me questions, but the media,” Castro said.

The Palace press office also said that Duterte’s remark was perhaps a reflection that “she’s so far behind.”

Article continues after this 

READ: Sara Duterte blames Marcos admin for rising debt, unemployment

“We have a saying, don’t we? The brain operates on a use it or lose it principle. So we’re not surprised if he’s a little behind on updates, current events, what the president and the government are doing, because she doesn’t know how to use a computer,” Castro said.

Article continues after this 

“So it seems she does not know how to research what is happening currently,” she added. /das

World.title: Ortega to Duterte on solons’ ‘money-making’ claim: Don’t play victim
World.content:
Sara Duterte (L) and Francisco Paolo Ortega V FILE PHOTOS

MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V asked Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday whether her camp had any “new fake news” to spread after she claimed lawmakers were profiting from the impeachment complaints filed against her.

In a statement, Ortega urged Duterte to stop “playing victim” and instead address the allegations raised against her, as outlined in the Articles of Impeachment prepared by the House committee on justice.

Article continues after this 

READ: 215 lawmakers back 2026 Duterte impeachment, matching 2025 tally – Ridon

Three days before the House vote on whether to impeach her, Duterte claimed that some lawmakers were allegedly making money from her name and suggested they should share the funds they supposedly receive with their constituents.

“That is already a worn-out and old argument. Whenever she is asked to answer the evidence, the response is immediately accusations that someone is earning money or receiving suitcases of cash. She should just answer the Articles of Impeachment,” Ortega said.

Ortega added that if Duterte believes there is no basis for impeachment, she should respond with “evidence, documents, and direct explanations,” instead of dismissing allegations involving P612.5 million in confidential funds, Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records, cash envelopes, and alleged threats.

According to Ortega, over 200 lawmakers have already signified their support to the Articles of Impeachment.

Article continues after this 

“If more than 200 lawmakers are ready to sign and if a large majority of the public wants a trial, then she can no longer say this is merely intrigue. This is no longer about her press statements. This is about evidence, accountability, and the proper constitutional process,” he said.

“What the people want is for her to face the allegations and answer them. The victim narrative and diversionary tactics will no longer work because the accusations are too serious and the amount of money involved is too large,” Ortega emphasized.

Article continues after this 

READ: NBI nabs PGMN founder Franco Mabanta for alleged extortion vs Romualdez

The vice president earlier claimed that some lawmakers were allegedly earning money from her impeachment and expressed hope that their constituents would also benefit from the supposed funds being distributed in “pockets or suitcases.”

Aside from Ortega, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon believes that Duterte will be impeached — no matter what she thinks or says.

“The Vice President is free to speak her mind as we head into the impeachment vote weekend. But the vote on Monday will happen, and she will be impeached for the second time under two different Congresses. We wish her the best,” Ridon said.

Last Monday, the House committee on justice approved the report containing the Articles of impeachment. It was filed before the House’s bills and index division and eventually brought to the plenary as Committee Report (CR) No. 261.

It was distributed to the House members on Wednesday.

READ: Articles of impeachment vs Sara Duterte reach House plenary

According to CR No. 261, the two complaints’ grounds were consolidated into four:

culpable violation of the Constitution, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust through the systematic liquidation, misuse, misappropriation, and irregular of confidential funds amounting to P500 million under the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and P112.5 million under the Department of Education (DepEd)

culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust when Duterte amassed unexplained wealth manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income and earnings during her incumbency as a public official

bribery, graft and corruption, culpable violation of the Constitution, and betrayal of public trust when she gave monetary gifts or payments to DepEd officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws

culpable violation of the Constitution, high crimes, and betrayal of public trust by contracting for the assassination of the President, the First Lady, and the former speaker of the House, by making grave threats, and by actively inciting sedition against the republic

READ: Secret funds, unexplained wealth: Duterte impeach articles cut to 4 grounds

The House is expected to deliberate and vote on the Articles of Impeachment on Monday. A one-third vote, or 106 out of the 218 members, is needed to elevate the case to the Senate.

Sources said the chamber could come close to or even match the 215 signatures gathered during the first impeachment bid against the vice president in 2025.

One insider who works closely with lawmakers believes there may be a lot of work to secure 200 affirmative votes, but it is possible.

Another source, meanwhile, said that they have already secured 200 signatures.

World.title: DILG chief Remulla eyes return to Cavite in 2028 polls: ‘I miss home’
World.content:
DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla (Photo from Jonvic Remulla Facebook page)

MANILA, Philippines — Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Friday said he is planning to return and seek an elective position in Cavite, his home province, in the 2028 elections.

“I miss home. This job is exhausting,” Remulla told reporters at the Kapihan ng Samahang Plaridel in Manila on Friday.

“My heart is set on going back to Cavite. We will cross the bridge when we get there,” he added.

Article continues after this 

READ: DILG chief Jonvic Remulla on 2028 polls: ‘Trabaho muna tayo’

Remulla, who previously served as Cavite governor, said he is open to a presidential bid, particularly if he were endorsed by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

After Vice President Sara Duterte formally declared her bid for the presidency last February, however, Remulla said he would rather “focus on work first.”

“I still have a wide perception gap na kailangan ko i-bridge. Iba pagkakaintindi nila sa akin (They read me differently.) Maybe there are other people that they think are more ready for the job. Tingin nila sa akin kasi burgis, elitista (They think I’m elitist.),” Remulla explained.

“What they don’t understand is that every single institution I’ve entered, I’ve always made it better,” he maintained. /gsg

World.title: P1.3-million ‘shabu,’ gun seized in Iloilo City raid
World.content:
Seized suspected “shabu” (crystal meth), a firearm, ammunition, and assorted drug paraphernalia, which were recovered during a police operation in Iloilo City that resulted in the arrest of a high-value drug suspect on Thursday, May 7, 2026. (Photo courtesy of Regional Police Drug Enforcement Unit)

ILOILO CITY — A high-value drug suspect was arrested during a search warrant operation that led to the seizure of over P1.3 million worth of suspected “shabu” (crystal meth) and an unlicensed firearm in Mandurriao district on Thursday morning.

The suspect, identified only by the alias “Romar,” 49, was apprehended at his residence in Zone 3, Barangay Pali Benedicto.

READ: Village watchman, welder nabbed with almost P1M in shabu in Iloilo

Article continues after this 

According to the Regional Police Drug Enforcement Unit (RPDEU)-6, the operation involved nearly two months of surveillance and monitoring. The search warrant was issued on May 5 by Branch 39 of the Regional Trial Court in Iloilo City.

Operatives recovered 30 heat-sealed transparent plastic sachets containing about 200 grams of suspected shabu with an estimated standard drug price of P1.36 million.

Authorities also seized a .38-caliber pistol loaded with four live rounds of ammunition, four improvised tooters, and assorted drug paraphernalia.

Police Brig. Gen. Josefino Ligan, director of Western Visayas police, commended the joint operatives from RPDEU-6, Iloilo City Police Office (ICPO) Police Station 5, Regional Intelligence Division-6, City Intelligence Unit, and the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) team for the successful operation.

“This successful operation reflects the strong commitment of our police personnel in protecting our communities from the harmful effects of illegal drugs and criminality,” Ligan said.

Article continues after this 

“The confiscation of these illegal substances and firearms prevented possible threats to public safety and saved many lives,” he added.

The suspect is currently detained at a police facility and faces charges for violations of Sections 11 and 12 of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, covering possession of dangerous drugs and drug paraphernalia.

Article continues after this 

READ: Iloilo City truck drivers nabbed for selling meth

Under Section 11 of the law, the offense carries a penalty of life imprisonment and a fine of up to P10 million.

World.title: NBI subpoenas PGMN’s CJ Hirro over alleged Romualdez extortion case

National Bureau of Investigation Director Atty. Melvin Matibag INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has issued a subpoena for Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN) anchor CJ Hirro over the alleged attempt to extort some P350 million from former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Hirro is expected to appear before the NBI headquarters in Pasay City on Monday, May 11.

On Thursday, Matibag said the NBI is considering Hirro a person of interest since she was mentioned in the complaint affidavit.

World.title: Borongan City hits dangerous 43°C heat index
World.content:
Borongan City in Eastern Samar recorded a heat index of 43 degrees Celsius on Friday, May 8, 2026, placing it under the “danger” category of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa). INQUIRER file image

TACLOBAN CITY- Borongan City in Eastern Samar recorded a heat index of 43 degrees Celsius on Friday, placing it under the “danger” category of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa).

This prompted health authorities to warn residents across Eastern Visayas against heat-related illnesses.

According to Pagasa, Borongan’s heat index on Friday matched Thursday’s 43°C reading and followed an even higher 45°C heat index recorded on Wednesday— the highest recorded in the city this week.

Article continues after this 

State weather bureau projections also showed Borongan may again experience a 43°C heat index on Saturday.

READ: 22 areas forecast to hit ‘danger’ level heat indices on Friday, May 8

Meanwhile, Tacloban City registered a 39°C heat index on Friday, classified by Pagasa under the “extreme caution” category.

As temperatures continue to rise across Eastern Visayas, the Department of Health-Eastern Visayas Center for Health Development (DOH-EVCHD) urged the public to take precautions against heat stroke and other heat-related illnesses.

“For your safety, the Department of Health-Eastern Visayas Center for Health Development reminds the public about health risks caused by extreme heat, such as heat stroke and other heat-related illnesses,” the agency said in an advisory.

Article continues after this 

READ: Here’s how to protect yourself from high heat index, according to DOH

The DOH said heat stroke may be caused by prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, strenuous physical activity in intense heat, dehydration, or lack of body fluids.

Article continues after this 

Health officials identified the early symptoms of heat stroke as headache, dizziness, vomiting, body weakness, pale skin, high fever or body temperature exceeding 41°C, loss of consciousness, and rapid heartbeat.

To prevent heat-related illnesses, the DOH advised the public to limit outdoor exposure; drink enough water to avoid dehydration; avoid tea, coffee, soft drinks, and alcoholic beverages; and use hats or umbrellas and wear light, loose clothing outdoors.

The agency also encouraged residents to schedule outdoor activities either early in the morning or later in the afternoon when temperatures are lower.

A heat index measures how hot it feels to the human body when relative humidity is combined with air temperature. Under Pagasa’s classification, a heat index between 42°C and 51°C falls under the “danger” level, where heat cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke become more likely with prolonged exposure or physical activity outdoors.

World.title: Police seek aggravated murder charge for main teen suspect in Yemanu Zelka killing
World.content:
The Israel Police said Friday it was seeking an aggravated murder charge for the main teenage suspect in the killing of 21-year-old Yemanu Binyamin Zelka.

Police said in a statement they had completed their investigation and would also recommend charges of joint enterprise murder and aggravated assault for several of the other suspects in the case.

The prosecutor’s office was expected to file the indictments early next week.

Zelka, a 21-year-old Pizza Hut employee in Petah Tikva, was stabbed to death by a group of adolescents on the eve of Independence Day, after he told them not to spray party foam in the restaurant.

After waiting outside for Zelka to finish his late-night shift, the youths ambushed and beat him, with one assailant taking out a knife and stabbing him. He died of his wounds a day later.

Get The Times of Israel's Daily Edition by email and never miss our top stories Newsletter email address Get it By signing up, you agree to the terms

On Monday, police confirmed that they had arrested all 19 minors suspected of involvement in the killing, after two weeks of searches.

According to Hebrew media, the âmain suspectâ in the case, believed to have carried out the stabbing, is a 15-year-old male. He turned himself in last week.

Since then, he was reportedly stonewalling interrogators, though a report last week said he broke his silence to say, âI didnât murder. I didnât stab.â



His parents were arrested on suspicion of tampering with the investigation, according to Channel 12.

The police statement on Friday confirmed that some suspects had sought to evade capture, and said that additional suspects had been arrested on suspicion of helping them, but it didn’t provide further details.

Channel 12 also reported this week that, during an interrogation, one of the other teenage suspects admitted to beating Zelka while he was on the ground, âjust trying to defend himselfâ amid the stabbing attack.

Asked why he’d continue to hit the victim — whom the interrogator described as “helpless” and “lying in a pool of blood” — the youth reportedly answered: âWhat should I do? Should I hit him and stop midway through? Everyone was hitting [him]. What? Should I stop?â

Zelkaâs killing came as a shock to many Israelis and spurred police to ramp up their efforts to combat juvenile delinquency, particularly in Tel Aviv and its environs.

World.title: LTC Nadav Shoshani: Is Israel telling the right story to the world?
World.content:
Welcome to The Times of Israel’s Lazar Focus. Each Friday, join hostÂ diplomatic correspondent Lazar Berman for a deep dive into what’s behind the news that spins the globe.

Israel has had a rough time of it on the international stage since the Hamas invasion of October 7, 2023, and the subsequent wars. Allegations of collective punishment, genocide, and targeting of religious sites have been made by some of Israel’s closest allies, and support for the Jewish state is plummeting in the West.

WATCH the full episode here:

Much of the criticism leveled at Israel, justified or not, revolves around what the world sees from the battlefield.

The IDF has a large, well-oiled public communications machine, and the IDF Spokesperson’s Unit does things other militaries can only dream of.

At the same time, there is a feeling in Israel and among its friends that the military is too slow and bureaucratic to effectively get its message out in the age of social media and AI.

LTC Nadav Shoshani, who returned to active duty in the wake of October 7, argues that despite Israel’s inherent disadvantages, the IDF is effectively communicating to the world.

In an interview the day before he steps down as the IDF’s international spokesman, Shoshani reveals his approach to speaking to the world about the war in Gaza.

He admits that Israel’s reputation is at a nadir and that the problem must be dealt with. Yet he stresses that Israel is facing structural disadvantages. Much of the world simply doesn’t like war. Israel’s enemies aren’t held to the same standard of truth and accuracy, which allows them to quickly spread lies while Israel is still carrying out investigations.

Shoshani lays out some of the lessons he’s learned in the position. Israel has to fill information vacuums, he says, even if it is a message that the country is investigating the incident at hand. He also opened many new social media accounts, in order “to be everywhere and to be active everywhere.”

Pressed on the persistent problem of IDF soldiers posting questionable content on social media, Shoshani says that he has invested significant effort into confronting it, with tangible results.

“They understand what’s happening,” says Shoshani. “They’re more sensitive. It’s still not where we want it to be, but it is much better.”

Shoshani takes listeners back to key episodes in the Gaza war, including the 2025 announcement by Defense Minister Israel Katz that nothing, including humanitarian aid, would be going into Gaza, and the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation fiasco in which Gazans were killed nearly daily around the food distribution sites.

He says that the IDF has acted properly around prisoners taken from Gaza. Shoshani visited the Sde Teiman base and says Hamas terrorists there are receiving food and medical care, and that there are lawyers onsite to make sure the guards adhere to the law.

Shoshani also argues that the IDF is doing everything it can to combat settler violence in the West Bank: “We see this as a core mission. Our mission in Judea and Samaria is to keep stability and to keep safety for all the people living in that area, to make sure there is no violence.”

The military recognizes the problem, he says, and is dealing with it, but it takes time.

Lazar Focus can be found on all podcast platforms. This episode was produced by Gabriella Jacobs and video edited by Ari Schlacht.
